chain_owns.not_proven: Economic activation, live receiver configuration, or hard finality.
chain_owns.source_claim: Payment identity is chain plus transaction hash plus log index; Base and Ethereum USDC are separate rails.

chain_owns.not_proven: Accepted-checkpoint finality, fork choice, or payment-to-fulfillment correlation.
chain_owns.source_claim: The delivery reconciler reads Chain-2050 chain ID, transaction receipt, and block number and verifies an exact VOID token transfer.

chain_owns.not_proven: One source payment to one Chain-2050 fulfillment as an on-chain invariant.
chain_owns.source_claim: Current delivery calldata is an ordinary ERC-20 transfer to address and amount; the source payment identity is not encoded in that transfer.

chain_owns.not_proven: A finalized Chain-2050 object or manifest commitment.
chain_owns.source_claim: Current field-object tooling creates and verifies SHA-256 content identities off-chain.

datanet_owns.required_property: At least one verified replica can return the exact bytes committed by the accepted anchor.
Replica claims remain availability evidence and cannot rewrite canonical object identity or ownership.
A retrieval route is accepted only after exact content verification; stale or malicious peers have zero truth authority.
Repair may copy verified bytes to a new replica but cannot manufacture or replace the chain anchor.
Local publication is failure-atomic, create-only, exact-generation bound, and preserves foreign replacements.

finality.current_limitation: The repository has a finalized API/helper response-file boundary, but its own documentation says it is not an actual live route call, fork choice, or peer quorum.

local_state_required.reason: Current Chain-2050 ERC-20 transfer calldata does not carry the source payment identity.
local_state_required.retirement: Retire only after source payment and Chain-2050 fulfillment are both accepted under their finality policies and a durable on-chain correlation anchor exists.

local_state_required.reason: A process may lose the transport result after broadcast and must reconcile without blindly resending.
local_state_required.retirement: Retire after the exact delivery transaction is proven confirmed/final or definitively not broadcast.

local_state_required.reason: It accelerates lookup and repair but does not define object truth.
local_state_required.retirement: May be discarded and rebuilt from accepted anchors plus verified peer inventory.

local_state_required.reason: Crash recovery must distinguish owned incomplete generations from foreign replacements.
local_state_required.retirement: Retire after exact bytes and manifest generation are durable or an owned failed generation is safely recovered.

recovery_algorithm.acceptance: Use chain, transaction hash, and log index; require the configured rail confirmation/finality policy.
Verify chain ID, token contract, fulfillment wallet, recipient, amount, transaction status, block identity, and current confirmation/finality policy.
Until an on-chain correlation anchor exists, use only a bounded exact-identity unresolved record; never promote it above either chain.
Reconstruct disposable object/replica indexes from accepted commitments and peer inventory.
Hash exact received bytes and accept only a match to the accepted object or manifest commitment.
Create-only publish verified replicas; a missing replica is availability loss, not a change in canonical truth.

conditional.condition: Retain only if a reviewed threat model proves byte-custody or unfinished-operation secrets require process isolation beyond ordinary least privilege.
Retain only for a compact local Datanet availability checkpoint or unfinished-operation root, never as a competing chain ledger.
Retain in bounded form until Chain-2050 records a deterministic one-payment-to-one-fulfillment anchor.

delete.reason: Finalized payment facts belong to the source payment chain.
Finalized delivery facts belong to Chain-2050.
A local status cache may project chain truth but may never contradict or replace it.
Crash recovery should query accepted chain state instead of replaying an independent local economic history.
The full payment-record cardinality belongs on the chains and must not remain a presale host-storage requirement.

retain.reason: Prevent partial or ambiguous byte generations after crash.
Preserve foreign or concurrent generations instead of overwriting them.
The bytes verified must be the bytes consumed.
Recovery cannot delete a replacement merely because an earlier pathname was owned.
Recovered bytes can be verified against an accepted commitment.
Unknown broadcast and incomplete publication states still need finite crash recovery.
